security_review: Customer OAuth return target is validated before the specialized login view can log out an authenticated SSO session.
Authenticated GET renders the native password form directly and does not log out; POST is CSRF-protected, no-store, and marks password parameters sensitive before dispatch.

Only the CSRF-valid POST to the validated customer reentry target logs out the prior SSO session before the library-native login flow. The allauth view retains password validation, rate limits, and the email-code stage.
Form posts back to the reentry endpoint with the redirect target, preserving the intended OAuth request through password and email-code stages.
Non-customer account-security reauthentication and staff/native security branches retain their prior route selection.
static_test_review: Added checks cover direct native form rendering, authenticated GET session preservation, CSRF rejection without logout, invalid target rejection without logout, wrong password without reuse of old SSO or email-code issuance, correct password requiring fresh email code, and same-user/exact-target completion.
Browser regression now expects the native password form directly after stale cabinet BFF session instead of an intermediate confirmation button.
limits: Read-only static review; no tests, production database, auth configuration, credentials, or host actions were used.
Candidate commit was not frozen at review time; the recorded file hashes and diff hash bind this review to the inspected worktree bytes.
CI qualification remains a separate gate.
